sourceChecks.excerpt: if there is an efficient (even imperfect) indistinguishability obfuscator, then there are one-way functions

sourceChecks.title: Everlasting UC Commitments from Fully Malicious PUFs
sourceChecks.excerpt: We present the first construction of an everlastingly UC-secure commitment scheme in the fully malicious token model
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A construction achieves everlasting UC commitment security assuming PUFs and a common reference string, and states a limitation for computation using non-erasable tokens.
sourceChecks.limitations: Hardware-assumption-based commitment result, not a practical general long-term data-protection system.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: practical everlasting security cryptographic commitments long term data protection primary

sourceChecks.title: On the Complexity of Verifiable Secret Sharing and Multiparty Computation
sourceChecks.excerpt: general MPC can only be black-box reduced efficiently to secret sharing if extra properties of the secret sharing scheme used
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Paper provides an information-theoretic VSS complexity result for general access structures and an impossibility result for efficient general MPC reductions.
sourceChecks.limitations: Does not establish constant communication overhead for information-theoretic MPC in general.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: information theoretic multiparty computation constant communication overhead cryptography primary

sourceChecks.title: RFC 9958: Post-Quantum Cryptography for Engineers
sourceChecks.excerpt: This shift may require significant protocol redesign due to the unique properties of post-quantum algorithms.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: IETF informational RFC covers standardized PQC algorithms and performance/security tradeoffs for KEMs and signatures.
sourceChecks.limitations: Does not establish simultaneously small keys and fast operations for every post-quantum public-key scheme.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: post quantum public key cryptography small key fast operations NIST standard primary specification

sourceChecks.title: FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard
sourceChecks.excerpt: SLH-DSA is based on SPHINCS+, which was selected for standardization as part of the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization process.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: NIST standardized a stateless hash-based post-quantum digital-signature algorithm.
sourceChecks.limitations: Standardization does not meet the proposed extremely small-signature and fast-verification combination; sizes and performance trade off.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: post quantum digital signature standard small signature fast verification size tradeoffs primary NIST

sourceChecks.title: On the Size of Pairing-Based Non-interactive Arguments
sourceChecks.excerpt: Our first contribution is a pairing-based (preprocessing) SNARK for arithmetic circuit satisfiability, which is an NP-complete language.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Groth’s pairing-based SNARK gives zero-knowledge proofs for an NP-complete circuit-satisfiability language using three group elements.
sourceChecks.limitations: Requires preprocessing and pairing assumptions/trusted setup; one concrete scheme, not a universal assumption-free proof platform.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: constant size succinct non-interactive zero knowledge proofs arbitrary NP statements Groth16 primary

sourceChecks.title: Practical Verified Computation with Streaming Interactive Proofs
sourceChecks.excerpt: Our general-purpose implementation is not yet practical for everyday use.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Paper implements general-purpose interactive verification for arbitrary computation, while emphasizing that this general implementation was not yet practical.
sourceChecks.limitations: The demonstrated implementation is bounded and interactive; it does not establish a fast non-interactive system for all arbitrary programs.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: verifiable computation arbitrary programs efficient secure proof general purpose primary research
